text:
mira: heads-up — saw a customer report where a ~1s streaming generation got retried mid-stream and the client ended up with duplicated overlapping text (second stream picked up mid-sentence). looks like gateway retried to fallback without any deterministic boundary. want to decide expected gateway contract for short-lived streams.
aj: can you dump the minimal headers/responses (redact ids)?
mira: pasted minimal trace: 
```:method: POST
:path: /v1/generate/stream
:authority: api.redwood.io
content-type: application/json
x-client: mobile-101
```
upstream closed connection after fragment 3/6. gateway opened new upstream to fallback model and forwarded remaining tokens. client saw fragments 1..3 then 3..6 (3 duplicated, overlapping sentence).
ryan: two axes: (A) gateway-transparent retry with strong dedupe semantics, or (B) explicit resume token managed either by client or created by gateway so resume is deterministic. Transparent dedupe is tricky for short streams.
sam: also flag side-effects. some customers trigger side-effecting callbacks mid-stream (rare but real). transparent retry risks double-side-effect. resume-token doesn't magically fix that unless the upstream is idempotent.
mira: agree. this incident was read-only but we should design for general case.
aj: sketching an approach:
- introduce an optional header `x-rw-enable-resume: true` clients send to opt into resume.
- gateway will emit trailer `x-rw-resume-token: <opaque>` on successful stream completion. token = HMAC(tenant, model, model-version, last-offset, expiry).
- on upstream transient, gateway will only attempt a transparent resume if the token is present and valid for the tenant/model and within TTL. otherwise gateway should fail the stream and return an error to the client.
- for hedged fanout (parallel model fallback), first-complete wins; gateway normalizes trailers to a single canonical set and attaches `x-rw-duplicate-dropped: true` for telemetry if another response was suppressed.
ryan: small refinements: use sequence-offsets rather than byte suffix to avoid encoding issues. e.g., token includes last-chunk-seq and a short HMAC. the gateway must ensure sequence monotonicity across retries.
sam: alternative: clients can include `x-rw-chunk-ack: seq` periodically so client-driven resume is possible. but that requires clients to change. maybe keep opt-in so we don't break PLG flows.
aj: performance note: generating HMAC per-stream might add 50-200us. for very short calls (<150ms) that's meaningful. we can make token generation lazy: only compute and attach if stream exceeds N chunks or time threshold.
mira: security: token must be scoped to tenant + model-version + connection id and TTL < 8s to avoid replay to other tenants. also consider binding to request nonce if supplied.
ryan: about hedging: if we fan-out and both responses produce output, gateway should not merge outputs; it should pick first-complete output stream and drop others. merging leads to interleaving. we can expose `x-rw-hedge-trace` in telemetry for debugging.
sam: billing & side-effects: we must document that resume opt-in is safe for read-only generation; side-effecting streams should set `x-rw-side-effect: true` (opt-in) and gateway will not retry for those. Dedicated customers might get a different default.
mira: ops impact: proxy pool must be able to persist ephemeral tokens for a few seconds if we want cross-node resume. easier: make token self-contained (stateless) so no cross-node persistence needed. but then token size includes last-offset and HMAC as noted.
aj: implement plan / action items:
- aj: draft RFC for `x-rw-enable-resume`, trailer contract, hedging canonicalization and `x-rw-side-effect` semantics. target Fri noon.
- ryan: prototype token HMAC + sequence offset and run microbench for latency impact (next sprint).
- sam: update billing & public docs with recommended defaults and side-effect guidance. determine tier defaults (PLG off, Dedicated on).
- mira: add e2e test criteria: duplicated-fragment assertion, hedge-suppression telemetry, and side-effect no-retry behavior.
ops-bot: ci-check — proxy-integration-tests queued (job id #3123) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
mira: temporary decision: opt-in resume via `x-rw-enable-resume` + gateway will only perform transparent single-resume attempt when token present. hedged fanout will keep first-complete canonical result. iterate after RFC. :+1:
aj: I'll include example curl + expected trailers in the RFC.
ryan: I'll post a short log sample for overlap-detection heuristics in the RFC to show why naive dedupe is brittle.
sam: booking RFC review slot on Fri 2pm.
mira: thanks everyone — close for now, will re-open if anything contradicts before RFC.
